data.name: Adith
data.gender_notes: Adith is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Adith is the name of the moon god in Hindu mythology. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'aditya', meaning 'bright'. Adith is also referred to as Soma or Chandra, representing the giver of light, knowledge, and prosperity. The name Adith carries the meaning “Bright, Moon” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Adith usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Adith belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bright, Moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adith total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The moon is considered a source of sustenance in Hinduism, as it affects the tides and thus plays a crucial role in the agricultural cycle. Adith, as the moon deity, is believed to bring life-giving rains and promote fertility. He is also a key player in various rituals and celebrations, such as the Chandra Nakshatras, which are based on the lunar phases.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Adith represents the inner light and constant source of knowledge and creativity within each individual. He is associated with truth, consciousness, and the never-ending cycle of birth, death, and rebirth. The transcendent aspects of Adith are embodied in the sage Agastya, who is believed to have tamed the divine energy of the moon. Thus, invoking the name Adith can inspire the seeker to connect with their inner radiance, intuition, and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Adith, meaning 'not the first', signifies the recognition of the cyclical nature of existence and the endless flow of time. It is a reminder that we are all part of this eternal dance and that there is no beginning or end to the journey of life.

historical_references.reference: Aditha is also a name of the goddess Aditi, who is the mother of the Adityas. She is the personification of the infinite and unmanifested cosmic power.
